questions.stem: Maternal Ab do NOT provide protective immunity to neonate against?
questions.solutionHtml:
Polio
  • The poliovirus causes polio. The virus enters the body through the mouth.
  • It is spread through contact with the feces (stool) of an infected person or through exposure to phlegm or mucus when an infected person coughs or sneezes.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 743

questions.stem: A 16-year-old female patient presents to the emergency department with features of typical pneumonia. Since the age of 6 months, she has had recurrent episodes of pneumonia and sinusitis due to Streptococcus pneumonia and Hemophilus influenza. Which component of immune function will be abnormal?
questions.solutionHtml:
B lymphocytes
  • Symptoms in question suggest a deficiency k/a common variable hypogammaglobulinemia, characterised by low serum level of IgG.
  • Here, the number of B cells is normal, but their ability to synthesise IgG and other immunoglobulins is severely compromised. Treatment involved gamma globulins to reduce the number of infections.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 85

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman comes to the hospital with c/o fever, chills, dysuria, and back pain. The symptoms started 6 days ago with burning on urination. Her temperature is 102 F. Physical examination shows left costovertebral tenderness. Urine analysis is positive for leukocytes and nitrites, which of the following Interleukins produced by macrophage is responsible for fever production by its action on hypothalamic cells:
questions.solutionHtml:
IL 1
  • Macrophages and other antigen-presenting cells produce IL 1. It is also known as endogenous pyrogen because of its direct on the hypothalamus.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition

questions.stem: Which of the following best denotes classical complement pathway activation in inflammatory immune condition:

options.label: B
options.text: C2 and C4 normal, C3 is decreased

options.label: C
options.text: C3 normal and C2 C4 decreased

options.label: D
options.text: C2, C4, C3 all are elevated

questions.solutionHtml:
C2, C4, C3 decreased
  • C2, C3 and C4 are specifically utilised in the classical pathway, hence their serum level will be low.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 205-210, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 164-66

questions.stem: Immunoglobulins (Ig) or antibodies are glycoproteins produced by plasma cells. B cells are instructed by specific immunogens, for example, bacterial proteins, to differentiate into plasma cells. Which of the following statements is true about an immunoglobulin?

options.label: A
options.text: IgG has max conc. in serum

options.label: B
options.text: IgM has max conc. in serum

options.label: C
options.text: IgA has max conc. in serum

options.label: D
options.text: IgE has max conc. in serum

questions.answerText: IgG has max conc. in serum
questions.solutionHtml:
IgG has max conc. in serum
  • Decreasing order of Serum levels of various immunoglobulin is G>A>M>D>E: The highest is IgG, and the lowest is Decreasing order of Serum level of IgG subtypes: IgG1>2>3>4


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 196-98, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 145-47

questions.stem: Which of the following precipitates at 50 to 60 DEGREE C but redissolve on heating:
questions.solutionHtml:
Bence Jones proteins
  • Abnormal immunoglobulin found in urine
  • Coagulates at 50oC, redissolves at 70oC
  • Elevated in Multiple myeloma
  • Produce excess light chains



Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No.199-201, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 147-49

questions.stem: Precipitation test is an antigen-antibody reaction in which the antigen forms in a solution. It is a test in which an antibody interacts with the soluble antigen in the presence of an electrolyte to produce a precipitate. Which one is the example of a gel precipitation test?
questions.solutionHtml:
Immunoelectrophoresis
  • Immunoelectrophoresis is a method for obtaining quicker results of immunodiffusion.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 228-229, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 153-54

questions.stem: Antigen-antibody interaction, or antigen-antibody reaction, is a specific chemical interaction between antibodies pro:
questions.solutionHtml:
Allotype
  • ALLOTYPES, or allelic variants within the constant regions, are known to exist for some of these isotypes and are inherited in a Mendelian co-dominant fashion in an allelic manner(“allelic type”).


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 201-2, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 148-151

questions.stem: Synthesis of immunoglobulin in membrane-bound or secretory form is determined by:

options.label: A
options.text: One turn to two turns joining rule

questions.solutionHtml:
Differential RNA processing
  • IgA is the predominant antibody in secretions whereas igE is associated with mast cell degranulation in allergic response.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 202, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 149-151

questions.stem: Immunoglobulin in Peyer’s patch is:
questions.solutionHtml:
IgA
  • Peyer’s patches are composed of 30-40 lymphoid follicles present in intestinal submucosa
  • They are required for intestinal secretory immunoglobulin A responses, which provide local or intestinal immunity or mucosal immunity.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 199, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 147

questions.stem: All are peripheral lymphoid organs except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Thymus
  • Central/ primary:- Thymus and Bursa of Fabricius (birds)/ Bone Marrow(human)


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 183, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 170-71

questions.stem: Common between B- and T-cells:

options.label: D
options.text: Perform both humoral and cellular immunity

questions.solutionHtml:
Origin from same cell lineage
  • Both T and B-cells originate from the same lymphoid progenitor cell lineage in the bone marrow.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 185-87, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 173-75

questions.stem: An immunologist is experimenting to understand precipitation reactions. He notes that on adding an excessive amount of antigen to a serum sample containing a small number of antibodies, the amount of precipitate formed is less. Whereas, when he added smaller amounts of antigen to the same sample, the precipitate formed more than the previous observation. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.solutionHtml:
Post Zone phenomenon

Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 107

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department after suffering an injury on her limbs from falling on the ground while playing with her friends. On examination, there was a large dirty wound covered with soil and bleeding. The doctor in charge decides to give the patient an injection of Tetanus immunoglobulin. Which of the following characteristics is not shown by this type of immunity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Long lasting
  • Giving pre-formed immunoglobulin directly is an example of acquired passive immunity which is not long-lasting.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 83,84

questions.stem: A student has a genetic defect and cannot produce the J chain, which is important in the structure of some immunoglobulin molecules. Which of the following will most likely be observed in this individual?

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease in mature B cells

options.label: B
options.text: A decrease in mature T lymphocytes

options.label: D
options.text: An increase in IgA in the intestine

questions.solutionHtml:
A decrease in serum IgM
  • Deficiency in the production of J chains for immunoglobulins could result in a decrease in serum IgA and IgM levels. These antibodies are dimers and pentamers of the basic immunoglobulin molecule and require a J chain to join the immunoglobulin chains.
  • There is no evidence that indicates that a deficiency in the production of J chains of IgA or IgM will cause a decrease in mature B cells, or T lymphocytes, an increase in serum IgM and a decrease in IgE, or a decrease in IgA (choices A, B, D).


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 99

questions.stem: Hapten is otherwise known as incomplete antigen Which of the following is true regarding a Hapten?

options.label: A
options.text: It is not Immunogenic but, Antigenic

options.label: B
options.text: It is both Immunogenic and Antigenic

options.label: C
options.text: It is Immunogenic but not Antigenic

options.label: D
options.text: It is neither Immunogenic nor Antigenic

questions.answerText: It is not Immunogenic but, Antigenic
questions.solutionHtml:
It is not Immunogenic but, Antigenic
  • Hapten is the incomplete antigen Which is Antigenic but not Immunogenic
  • It is conjugated with a protein and induces Immunogenicity


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 134

questions.stem: A is a property of antigen Which is the ability to induce an immune response to a host (antibodies are formed against antigen). B is the property of antigen Which is the ability to bind with a specific antibody. A and B properties of an antigen are, respectively?
questions.solutionHtml:
Immunogenicity and antigenicity

Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 128

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true regarding T cell-independent antigen?

options.label: A
options.text: Antigen directly activates B Cell, which results in polyclonal activation

options.label: B
options.text: Antigen-presenting cell processes the antigen and presents the Antigenic peptides molecules on its surface to T helper cells

options.label: C
options.text: Polyclonal activation of B Cells results in the production of antibodies and exaggerated immune response

options.label: D
options.text: All the above statements are true regarding a T Cell independent antigen

questions.answerText: Antigen-presenting cell processes the antigen and presents the Antigenic peptides molecules on its surface to T helper cells
questions.solutionHtml:
Antigen-presenting cell processes the antigen and presents the Antigenic peptides molecules on its surface to T helper cells

Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 141

questions.stem: When two organisms share the same antigen, the same antibody can bind to both antigens. The antigen in this immunological mechanism is known as:
questions.solutionHtml:
Heterophile antigen
  • Heterophile antigen is an antigen shared by two different organisms Which therefore results in binding to the same antibody
  • This immunological mechanism is the basis of heterophile agglutination tests like Paul Bunnell test /Weil Felix reaction etc.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 132

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presented to the outpatient clinic with complaints of fever, cold, cough, myalgia, headache since 5 days. The attending physician advised antibody testing. Antibody-secreting plasma cells are derived from?
questions.solutionHtml:
B Cells
  • Plasma cells are derived from terminally differentiated B Cells, which have an important role in antibody secretion.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 135

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male presented with fever, cough, cold, chills and shortness of breath. The condition of the patient is caused by streptococcus pneumoniae. Pneumococcal is a capsulated bacterium that has c carbohydrate antigen in it, which is a T Cell independent antigen. All the following are true regarding c carbohydrate antigen except?

options.label: A
options.text: It has lower Immunogenicity than protein antigen

options.label: B
options.text: It can cause polyclonal B Cell Activation

options.label: C
options.text: Does not require stimulation by T Cells

questions.solutionHtml:
Memory response is present
  • T Cell independent antigen directly activates B Cells and results in polyclonal activation antibody production and exaggerated immune response.
  • Since they do not require T Cell activation, that does not have any memory.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 132

questions.stem: A 43-year-old male inmate with stage C3 HIV/AIDS presents with loose, watery stools, abdominal cramping, sweats, fevers, poor appetite (2 months) and 15 lbs. weight loss. He is taking Tenofovir one tablet bid and Nelfinavir 1,000 mg tid, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole for secondary pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP) prophylaxis. He reports good adherence, with an undetectable viral load and a CD4 count of 100 cells/mm3. All the following are the functions of CD4 cells except?

options.label: A
options.text: They play an important role in Immunogenic memory

questions.solutionHtml:
Production of immunoglobulins

Immunoglobulin production is the function of plasma cells Which are derived from differentiated B Cells



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 140
